Requisition

/rek-wih-ZISH-un/ - the stress falls on ZISH · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Requisition means a formal demand for goods or property made by an authority.

A requisition arrived by motorcycle at dawn: every ferry on the lake now answered to the army.

Worked Example

The letter that closed the school reads politely and offers no choices. By order of the district commander, the gymnasium and both classroom wings would receive two hundred convalescent soldiers on Friday; desks were to be stacked in the yard; the boiler would be kept lit at the army's expense. A receipt was enclosed. The headmistress filed it, as instructed, under R.

Requisition is the exact word for that letter, because a requisition is a formal demand for goods or property made by an authority — the courtesies of a request with none of its freedom. A seizure would simply have taken the building; the requisition documents the taking, names a rate, and files the paperwork, which changes the tone but not the outcome.

How Requisition Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

seizure

seizure: takes the thing outright, no receipt and no rate

levy

levy: the demand measured out in money or men; a requisition names the goods themselves

Antonyms

donation

donation: handed over freely, unasked

purchase

purchase: taken only at a price the owner agreed to

How Strong Is It? — request → requisition → confiscation

request vs. requisition

request vs. requisition: A request leaves the choice on your side of the counter — no is a complete answer.

confiscation vs. requisition

confiscation vs. requisition: Confiscation goes further than requisition — a requisition takes your trucks against a receipt and a rate; confiscation takes them and calls them the state's.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of requisition.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: back, insistently

Root — quisit

Root — quisit: to seek, to demand (Latin quaerere, quaesitus)

Suffix — -ion

Suffix — -ion: the act of

Put it together

Put it together: Re- (insistently) + quisit (to seek) + -ion (the act of) = the act of seeking and insisting. Latin requirere meant to seek out and demand, and its participle requisitus hardened into the official's noun: the seeking done on paper, under a seal, to which the only listed answer is yes.

Use the root in a new word: inquisitive

Use the root in a new word: inquisitive: An inquisitive mind runs the same seeking root the pleasant way around — in-, into everything, question after question.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / bureaucratic

Requisition is supply-office language — armies, emergencies, quartermasters — and the paper matters: it is a demand wearing a form's clothing. A request can be refused; a levy is counted in money or conscripts; a seizure or confiscation drops the paperwork and just takes. In an office the word lives a tamer life: you requisition staplers, and the only casualty is a budget line.
